reason: Conversation 2 picked up the key clue (cycle interrupted by pulling the plug), correctly identified the heater/thermal cut-out as likely, guided a safe unplugged top-panel look, and escalated sensibly to an engineer for continuity testing once she had no meter. Conversation 1 injected a false 'supply trip hazard' safety warning that contradicted the customer, repeatedly confused her, never got the filter question answered usefully, and never used the interrupted-cycle fact. Its final advice to get an engineer is acceptable, but it rests on an invented hazard rather than sound diagnosis.
